subject: Multitenancy isolation scenarios - SOC2 evidence request
messages:
From: Maya Rao <security@acme-corp.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tim Nguyen <tim@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Request: isolation scenarios + diagram package for SOC 2 audit

Connor —

Thanks for taking this. Our SOC 2 auditor has asked for a focused package describing how Redwood handles tenant isolation across Dedicated and Private deployments. Specifically they asked for: 

- network diagrams showing tenant overlays, NAT/egress points, and KMS boundaries for both Dedicated (shared rack/pool) and Private (customer VPC/on-prem) modes
- a "scenario matrix" mapping attacker/tenant failure modes (misconfigured routing, cross-tenant egress, compromised VM) to controls and tests performed
- evidence extracts for egress filtering rules, and any microsegmentation policy names/IDs
- statements on whether physical or logical isolation is used, and how fallback routing is handled when capacity is constrained

Can you send an initial bundle by end of next week? If you have a short meeting with your security lead to walk the auditor through the diagrams that would be helpful — auditor's availability: Oct 27-29 (PST).

Appreciate it — the auditor is focused on clear artifacts and traceable evidence.

Maya Rao
Director, Security Assurance
Acme Corp

Thanks for the clear list. We can produce an annotated diagram set and the scenario matrix you described. Plan:

- I will assemble an initial package (diagram + scenario matrix + evidence extracts) and share a Drive link by Oct 22.
- Karthik (security) will provide the control mapping and redacted evidence extracts.
- We can schedule a 30-min walkthrough for Oct 27; are mornings PST ok?

Looping in Karthik to confirm scope and timelines — Karthik, please see Maya's ask below and confirm whether the auditor needs packet captures or if ACL/policy exports and screenshots suffice.

Connor O'Brien

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: SOC2 materials for Acme — deliverables and owners

Team —

Acme's auditor requested a focused package for tenant isolation across Dedicated and Private. Deliverables we should prepare: 

1) Annotated network diagrams (two flavours):
   - Dedicated: overlay + physical host/pool boundaries, NAT/egress points, default and fallback routing paths
   - Private: VPC/on-prem mapping, customer-managed subnets, peering/VPN termination points

2) Multitenancy scenario matrix (xlsx): examples of failure/attack scenarios mapped to controls, test evidence, and responsible owner (SOC2 control IDs if possible)

3) Evidence extracts: ACL dumps, iptables/NSG snippets (redacted), policy IDs, KMS key ACL summary, and one representative microsegmentation policy (if used)

4) Short narrative (1 page) that states whether we use physical segregation options (Dedicated reserved pools) vs logical overlay approaches and where fallbacks occur

Who: Karthik — primary on technical narrative + evidence extracts. Lauren — review diagrams and matrix for clarity. Ben — grab the policy export for Dedicated egress rules and confirm names.

Target: initial package by 2026-10-22 EOD. If we need extra time for packet captures, propose that separately.

Thanks — Connor

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-20T12:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: SOC2 materials for Acme — deliverables and owners

Connor / team —

Acknowledged. Quick clarifications before we assemble: 

- Auditor asks specifically whether Acme expects a physical tenant-per-pool guarantee for Dedicated, or if logical tenant fencing (VLAN/overlay + kernel isolation) is acceptable. We should call out both options and where each is offered (e.g., reserved GPU pool for enterprise Dedicated customers vs shared Dedicated pools for standard tier).

- For evidence: screenshots and exported policy files (NSG/iptables, ipset lists) are typically sufficient. Packet captures are rarely requested and add complexity; we'll offer them as optional follow-up with redaction.

- KMS: we'll provide a summarized KMS access policy (key alias, roles allowed) and a short note on CMK rotation frequency. We must avoid exporting raw key material or any HSM logs.

- Fall back routing: include the policy name that triggers fallback to regional-compatible model variants and the audit log path for when fallback occurred (we can point to a log index id — not raw logs).

I'll prepare: annotated diagram layers (PNG & PDF), scenario matrix (xlsx), redacted policy exports (.txt), and a 1-page narrative (PDF). Expect initial ZIP link by Oct 22 morning.

Karthik
Principal Security Engineer

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.ai>
To: Maya Rao <security@acme-corp.com>, Tim Nguyen <tim@acme-corp.com>

Date: 2026-10-21T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Deliverable: multitenancy isolation package (initial) — Acme SOC 2 request

Maya / Tim —

Attached is the initial package for the auditor: 

Attachments (zipped):
- redwood-multitenancy-diagram-v2.pdf (annotated diagrams: Dedicated + Private overlays)
- multitenancy-scenario-matrix.xlsx (failure modes mapped to controls and test evidence)
- egress-policy-extracts.txt (redacted ACL/NSG exports)
- kms-boundary-notes.pdf (KMS access summary, rotation cadence)

Quick notes: 
- Dedicated: where customers purchase a reserved pool we can guarantee no co-located tenants on the same host; standard Dedicated pools are logically isolated with VLAN/overlay and kernel-level namespaces. Both models are documented in the PDF.
- Private: diagrams show common patterns for VPC peering, VPN termination, and customer-managed egress NAT. We call out how our router fallback policies are triggered and where the audit trail is captured.

Links: package in our shared Drive (view-only) — https://drive.google.com/redwood/acme/multitenancy-package
Related ticket: SUP-2345 (internal) — created to track any additional evidence requests. HubSpot record: HS-9987.

Please confirm if the auditor needs packet captures or raw logs; we prefer to provide exported policy files and redacted extracts first and handle deeper requests by exception.

If this meets the audit intake, we can schedule a 30-min walkthrough on Oct 27 morning PST — propose Oct 27 at 09:30 PT.

Best —
Connor O'Brien
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
